Assassin

Role: Melee DPS. Difficulty: Hard. Weapon: Dual Dagger (sword or bow noted as secondary/off options by some guides).

DPSMeleeHigh skill ceiling

blocks.title: Overview and role
blocks.headExtrasHtml: contested kr-era marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
Assassin is a hard, high-ceiling melee striker: stealth in, burst from behind, then disengage.

The Assassin is a melee DPS class wielding daggers, with dual-dagger as the core setup and sword or bow noted as secondary/off options by some guides Fextralife, date unknown1 aion2hub, date unknown2.

Playstyle

It plays as a hit-and-run striker:

  1. Open from stealth with Ambush or Shadowstrike.
  2. Unload a fast dagger combo, Quick Slice and Flash Slice, for back-attack burst.
  3. Disengage or weave defensively with Evasion Stance.

This phrasing appears near-verbatim across sources (confirmed) aion2hub, date unknown3.

Difficulty

Rated Hard by at least one general beginner guide, which calls Assassin "suited for experienced players who enjoy positioning" and "not recommended for new players due to their high skill floor" Overgear, date unknown4.

A separate class-explainer source calls Assassin the class with the highest skill ceiling and an active melee combo game timesaver, date unknown5.

Confirmed by two independent sources that this is not a beginner-friendly class, so expect a learning curve around positioning and animation-canceling.

PvE standing (contested)

Top PvE burst

  • Considered the best PvE class for clearing content per early focus-group-test (FGT) player rankings, ahead of Ranger aion2hub, date unknown6

Weaker sustained parse

  • Gains more from a short PvP engagement than from standing on a boss for an extended damage test, implying weaker sustained PvE parse damage relative to ranged casters exitlag, date unknown7

Treat Assassin as strong-to-top PvE burst but not the most forgiving sustained-DPS pick.

PvP standing

Multiple sources describe Assassin as a top-tier PvP class.

  • "Was the KR launch problem child, too strong. Nerfs brought it back to earth. It's still top-tier PvP, just no longer unfair." kr-era ggwtb, date unknown8
    • Strengths: heavy burst, stealth engages, gap closers. Weaknesses: unforgiving punishment for bad openers, real melee risk.
  • A Season 2 balance pass reportedly buffed Assassin further for both PvE and PvP, improving its standing in new endgame dungeons and the Abyss (same source, KR-era, subject to change before global launch)

Party demand: Assassin falls under "damage" roles rather than the guaranteed party-demand roles held by Templar/Cleric/Chanter-type support and tank classes. It is wanted for burst but is not an auto-invite the way support classes are ggwtb, date unknown9.

Who should pick it: players who enjoy tight positioning, animation-cancel timing, and a high-risk/high-reward melee duelist playstyle, and who accept a rougher early learning curve for a strong PvP ceiling and competitive-to-top PvE burst.

blocks.title: Skill priority
blocks.headExtrasHtml: contested kr-era marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
Bring Quick Slice, Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion, and Savage Roar to level 20 first.

Early leveling priority (single source, detailed): Quick Slash, Roar of the Beast, Ambush, Surprise Attack, and Pattern Explosion are named as the foundational early kit, with emphasis on mastering normal-attack canceling, left-click a normal attack then right-click a skill quickly to remove animation delay Vortex Gaming, date unknown1 kr-era.

  1. Bring to level 20 first: Quick Slice, Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion, Savage Roar Field Manual, date unknown2
  2. Secondary/flex skills: Storm Rampage (lvl 16), Shadow Fall (lvl 12+), Whirlwind Slice (lvl 12/16), Flash Slice (lvl 8+), Infiltrate (lvl 8+), Defiance (lvl 12/16) Field Manual, date unknown3
  3. Passive priority order: Rear Smite, then Assault Stance, then Exploit Weakness, then Impact Hit (confirmed, two independent extractions of the same source agree)
Avoid: spreading Skill Points across all abilities instead of committing to the core breakpoint skills; this is called out as a known beginner mistake pvpbank, date unknown4.

Mastery/chain skills: Assassin uses a "chain system" where skills connect into one another to extend combos for higher DPS or utility such as pulls, stuns, and lifesteal via chained follow-ups u4gm, date unknown5 (single source, could not verify by direct fetch, 403).

Pattern-first (before mastery complete)

  • Pattern Explosion into Heart Gore/Heart Stab, argued as better before your mastery investment is finished Inven, date unknown6 kr-era

Heart-first (after mastery complete)

  • Heart Gore/Heart Stab into Pattern Explosion, argued as better once mastery investment is finished (same KR thread, contested ordering) kr-era
Skill names vary by translation: "Heart Gore," "Heart Stab," and "Heart" (as in "Heart normal-attack cancel") likely refer to the same or a closely related skill across scraped guides. Flagged as contested naming rather than confirmed identical.

blocks.title: Leveling build
blocks.headExtrasHtml: Lv 1 to cap contested kr-era
blocks.bodyHtml:
Push Heart Pierce and Pattern Explosion to skill Lv 16 first, then lock in Triniel's Dagger as your first stigma.

This order comes from Korean Inven Assassin board consensus across several live-server posts, cross-checked against an English fan site that instead targets skill Lv 20 Inven, 2025-111 Field Manual, date unknown2. Every target below is the skill's own level, its 8/12/16/20 breakpoints, not your character level, since no source ties a step to one.

Skill point order

StepWhenSkillTake toWhySrc
1From Lv 1Quick Strike (빠른베기)Early, ongoingbuilt-in lifesteal, used constantlyInven, 2025-11 Inven, date unknown
2NextHeart Pierce (심장찌르기)Skill Lv 16crit resets cooldown, restores mental forceInven, 2025-11 Inven, date unknown
3NextPattern Explosion (문양폭발)Skill Lv 16detonates rune stacks, cooldown toolInven, date unknown Inven, 2025-11
4At Lv 23 (Stigma unlock)Triniel's Dagger stigma10 pointslocks in the cooldown-reduction backboneInven, 2025-11
5When points allowAmbush/Surprise AttackSkill Lv 16-20target is personal preference post-patchInven, 2026-01 Inven, date unknown
6Remaining pointsWhirlwind Cut and InfiltrateSkill Lv 20viable fillers, playstyle-dependentInven, 2026-01

KR consensus target: skill Lv 16

  • Matches the Skill Point budget an actual leveling character has Inven, date unknown3

Field Manual target: skill Lv 20

  • Core four, Quick Slice, Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion, Savage Roar, to 20 before any stagger, recovery, or movement skill Field Manual, date unknown4
  • Then Storm Rampage to 16, Shadow Fall to 12+, Whirlwind Slice/Defiance to 12/16, Flash Slice/Infiltrate to 8+ Field Manual, date unknown5

For pure leveling, follow the KR consensus. Skill Lv 20 needs Daevanion plus Arcana investment that only becomes realistic post-45, so treat the Field Manual's core-four-to-20 order as an endgame target, not a leveling goal Field Manual, date unknown6.

Passives

  1. First: Rear Smite, also named Backstab in the Korean order below, very likely the same passive under different translations Field Manual, date unknown7 Inven, 2026-018
  2. Then, English order: Assault Stance, Exploit Weakness, Impact Hit, see Skill priority above Field Manual, date unknown9
  3. Korean order instead: Defense Crack, Exploit Opening, unreconciled with the English list Inven, 2026-0110

Level by level

  1. Lv 1-12
    Push the lifesteal chain, animation-cancel from the start

    A weak early investment in Quick Strike makes leveling feel clunky, see Rotation and combos below for the opener Inven, 2025-1111.

  2. Lv 12
    Daevanion opens, two cooldown nodes first on Nezekan

    Then cheap attack/crit tiles toward the orange node; by around Lv 20 you should fund two core nodes each on Nezekan and Zikel Inven, date unknown12.

  3. Lv 23
    Stigma unlocks, two orders disagree on the first pick

    Illusive Clone first, then Triniel's Dagger Field Manual, date unknown13, or Beast Fangs first per a separate six-slot list DCInside, date unknown14.

    • Both orders still agree Triniel's Dagger and Illusive/Shadow Clone belong in the first few picks, see the note below
  4. Lv 23-45
    Main story and orange quests are the primary leveling path

    Keep the beginner PvE weave from Rotation and combos running as points and shards fill in around it Field Manual, date unknown15.

  5. Lv 45+
    Shift to farming Daevanion and Lord-trace points

    Weekly loop of Wanted Order quests, Abyss accessories, expedition gear, and Transcendence Arcana Field Manual, date unknown16.

  6. At cap
    Hand-off: grow into the skill Lv 20 core four

    See Skill priority above, and Stigma picks and Daevanion board route below, for the full endgame spread.

No separate "Leave at level 1" or "Gear while leveling" block: no source names a skill to leave at 1, and the gear enhancement order is the one under Gear and stat priority below.

Daevanion unlock level is contested: the class note gives Nezekan at character Lv 12, but a search-aggregated summary of a separate Inven post instead says Nezekan at Lv 10 and Zikel at Lv 20, lower-confidence since the direct fetch failed Inven, date unknown17. Stigma fill order is likewise contested, Illusive Clone first versus Beast Fangs first, though both agree Triniel's Dagger and Illusive/Shadow Clone belong early DCInside, date unknown18; a live player thread shows this exact trade-off in practice, asking whether to lower Swift Contract to fund Triniel's Dagger, with no visible resolution Inven, date unknown19.

blocks.title: Stigma picks
blocks.headExtrasHtml: First core set at unlock and shortly after confirmed marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
Illusive Clone, Swift Contract, Triniel's Dagger, and Savage Fang form the core stigma kit.

Core kit (unlock and shortly after)

The most consistently recommended kit keeps major cooldowns together, gives room for defensive play, and performs well without a perfect run, with Evasion Stance as a common defensive pick for the flexible slot pvpbank, date unknown1 Field Manual, date unknown2.

  • Illusive/Illusion Clone
  • Swift Contract (also seen as "Contract of Swiftness")
  • Triniel's Dagger
  • Savage Fang

Confirmed across 2+ independent sources for the core four.

  • Triniel's Dagger is repeatedly called the cornerstone stigma, reducing overall skill cooldown at level 10, or roughly 10% recast reduction on hit per one phrasing Vortex Gaming, date unknown3 kr-era Field Manual, date unknown4.
  • Illusive Clone is separately named as the stigma with the single biggest damage impact, top priority for Stigma Shard investment Vortex Gaming, date unknown5.
    • Also called "Phantom Clone" in one search summary.
    • Naming is inconsistent between "Illusive Clone," "Illusion Clone," and "Phantom Clone" across scraped guides, contested naming, likely the same skill.
  • Additional/situational stigmas Vortex Gaming, date unknown6 Field Manual, date unknown7:
    • Beast's Fang: reduces boss groggy gauge, useful for PvE boss fights
    • Dark Throw: reduces enemy movement speed, PvP utility
    • Throw Shadowblade: ranged damage option for the flex slot

PvE vs PvP: one source explicitly separates the two, noting PvE stigma priority favors mana recovery, lifesteal, and cooldown reduction for rune-detonation skills to sustain damage through longer fights, while PvP favors stealth uptime and stun-duration extension for control pvpbank, date unknown8.

Spend Stigma Shards first on: Illusive/Phantom Clone (highest damage impact per source), then Triniel's Dagger to lock in the cooldown-reduction backbone. Single-source ordering, but the two skills are consistently paired across guides.
blocks.tags: assassin stigma shards illusive clone triniel

blocks.title: Daevanion board route
blocks.headExtrasHtml: First board unlocks lvl 12 contested single source
blocks.bodyHtml:
Boards unlock through level 45; sources disagree whether there are 6 or 8 total.

Board count (contested)

The Daevanion board unlocks progressively by level.

  • One wiki source lists six boards: Nezekan (Lv 12), Zikel (Lv 20), Vaizel (Lv 30), Triniel (Lv 40), Ariel (Lv 45), Azphel (Lv 45) Fextralife, date unknown1
  • A separate search summary additionally names Marchutan and Yustiel as advanced level-45 boards, for eight total Fextralife, date unknown2

Sources disagree on whether there are 6 or 8 total boards, possibly a page update or a KR/TW-versus-global difference.

Node types: grey nodes are stat increases (lowest point cost), green nodes level up passive skills, blue nodes level up active skills, and orange/unique nodes grant special effects (highest point cost) Fextralife, date unknown3. This matches the blue-active/green-passive framing used elsewhere in this guide (confirmed).

  1. Lv 12
    Nezekan board unlocks

    Recommended route: prioritize hitting skill-level breakpoints (12/16/20) over the cheapest tile; ignore point-cost order when a lower-rarity tile completes a breakpoint Field Manual, date unknown4 (single source).

  2. Post-breakpoints
    Stat-node order

    Attack, then Critical Hit/Accuracy, then HP, then Defense (single source).

Points and farming

Daevanion Points are earned through general progression and account/character milestones. No AION 2-specific source gave a precise farming list beyond "you will eventually get enough Daevanion Points to cover the entirety of the boards" Fextralife, date unknown5.

Post-45 progression involves collecting Lord-trace skill points and farming Daevanion points from sealed/endgame content Field Manual, date unknown6 (single source).

Reset cost

kr-era, single source, flagged by the source itself as provisional The only concrete reset cost figure found is a cross-class one, not confirmed Assassin-specific: a Korean patch reportedly set individual Daevanion node resets to 500 Kinah, with the client also supporting a full board reset.

A dependency rule applies: a node cannot be removed if another already-acquired node depends on it. The source explicitly warns the number could change for global expcarry, date unknown7.

When to reset, and whether 500 Kinah is Assassin-specific: no reliable source found. A Korean search on "살성 데바니온 초기화 비용" (Assassin Daevanion reset cost) turns up only general discussion of counting activated nodes to estimate total Daevanion Crystal needs before a reset, with no Assassin-specific cost figure contested/unclear fmkorea, date unknown8. Net: reset cost is likely the same 500 Kinah per node cross-class figure, but no second source confirms it is Assassin-specific or unchanged, treat as unconfirmed for Assassin specifically.

blocks.title: Arcana
blocks.headExtrasHtml: single source kr-era marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
No independently confirmed Assassin Arcana mapping; a Scroll/Compass/Chalice/Scales order is documented.

How Arcana works (general)

Arcana cards are equipped in card slots to gain Combat Power, passive/active skill bonuses, skill-level "transcendence" past normal caps, set effects, and stat amplification Vortex Gaming, date unknown1 kr-era expcarry, date unknown2.

To push a skill to level 20: Daevanion (4) plus Arcana (4) equals 18, with the remaining 2 points from ring slots that can each carry one active-skill line Vortex Gaming, date unknown3 (single source, unverified independently).

Assassin-specific slotting (single source, fan-made)

A suggested high-end upgrade order, current through 2026-08-12 per the site itself Field Manual, date unknown4:

  • Scroll: main active-skill trio (Quick Slice, Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion) in a 4/2 or 3/3/2 level split
  • Compass: secondary actives Savage Roar, Storm Rampage, and Defiance
  • Chalice / Scales: pushes passive skill levels (Rear Smite, Assault Stance, Exploit Weakness)
  • Key/Hourglass slot: offense favors Weapon Damage; Hourglass is "acceptable with PvE resistance"
Gap remains, single source confirmed: no independent confirmation of this card-to-skill mapping exists; other sources surface only generic, non-Assassin-specific Arcana explainers covering card types and general Frenzy/Purity/Libra combos, with no independently-authored Assassin-specific card mapping found still single source mmoexp, date unknown5. Treat these exact card-to-skill assignments with caution until a second source turns up.
What to avoid: no reliable source explicitly listed Arcana cards or configurations Assassin should avoid. General Arcana guides mention that older "meta" configurations (4 Vitality/1 Magic) have been superseded by newer mixes (3 Vitality/2 Magic or 2 Vitality/3 Magic), but this was not tied specifically to Assassin Vortex Gaming, date unknown6 kr-era.

blocks.title: Gear and stat priority
blocks.bodyHtml:
Stack Critical Hit, Attack, and Accuracy/Penetration; enhance the weapon slot first.

Weapon: Dagger (dual-wield is the core identity). One PvP-focused source suggests a Sword (Main) plus Dagger (Off) combination specifically for PvP burst and stun-duration extension u4gm, date unknown1 (single source, unverified by direct fetch).

  1. Top stats: Critical Hit, Attack (or Attack Speed), Accuracy/Penetration pvpbank, date unknown2
  2. Secondary: Evasion, as a defensive stat named by one source
  3. Example PvE Crit-DPS build: a sample high-crit gear loadout aion2hub, date unknown3
    • Critical Hit 1,739, Attack 3,053, Penetration 1,830, Defense 13,338
    • PvE Damage Boost 33.5%
    • From a community build using an Archon Praetorian Captain Dagger (+20 enchant, +5 exceed) and a full Splendent Nemesis Dragon Lord armor set. Treat as an example, not a universal target.

Per-slot enhancement priority (single source, fan-made)

A separate fan-made source gives this order Field Manual, date unknown4 (single source):

  1. Weapon first: Combat Speed, Might, then Weapon Damage Boost, then Damage Boost
  2. Helmet: Smite plus Attack Increase
  3. Pauldrons: Critical Damage Boost
  4. Chest: Damage Boost
  5. Pants: Damage Tolerance plus Attack Increase
  6. Gloves: Combat Speed
  7. Cloak: Smite plus Attack Increase
  8. Shoes: Movement Speed
  9. Jewelry: Attack first, Critical Hit once an accuracy hit-check threshold is met

The same source gives a manastone-equivalent order: Back Attack Boost, then Weapon Damage Boost, then Critical Damage Boost, then Attack +25/+30, then Damage Boost.

Which piece to enhance first: the weapon, per the Field Manual source above (single source), consistent with general MMO practice of prioritizing main-hand weapon enchant/enhance for DPS classes.
Set effects: "Splendent Nemesis Dragon Lord" appears as a named armor set in the example PvE build, described only by its stat contributions rather than an explicit set-bonus description aion2hub, date unknown5 (single source).

blocks.title: Rotation and combos
blocks.headExtrasHtml: single source kr-era marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
Open from stealth with Ambush, weave normal-attack cancels, and finish with Pattern Explosion.

Beginner PvE rotation

Open with Ambush, normal-attack-cancel, Surprise Attack, normal-attack-cancel, Heart (Gore/Stab), normal-attack-cancel, Pattern Explosion, repeating the animation-cancel weave throughout kr-era Vortex Gaming, date unknown1.

A separate source frames the loop as maintain rune stacks, detonate with Pattern Explosion at max stacks, weave Quick Slash for mana sustain pvpbank, date unknown2.

  1. Pop Illusive Clone, Swift Contract, and Savage Fang together Field Manual, date unknown3 (single source)
  2. Follow with Triniel's Dagger
  3. Run your four core rear-positioned attacks during the resulting buff window
  4. If Illusive Clone is on cooldown, deploy Storm Rampage during a boss's stagger/groggy window instead
Buff timing: hold Triniel's Dagger for only 3-8 seconds to keep buff alignment tight (single source).

PvP opener

Stealth only right before engaging, to avoid wasting duration. Open with Ambush from behind for the maximum damage multiplier, chain into Surprise Attack, and finish with Pattern Explosion pvpbank, date unknown4 (single source).

A separate PvP combo listing gives: Illusion Clone buff, Ambush, Shadow Fall, Wide Slash, Triniel's Dagger plus Ambush kr-era Vortex Gaming, date unknown5.

Defensive/utility cooldowns: Evasion Stance and Shadow Walk (a stealth-based defensive/repositioning tool) are named as the class's core defensive kit, used to avoid downtime during rotation rather than only reactively Fextralife, date unknown6 Field Manual, date unknown7.

Auto-hunt/macro setup: a Korean-language thread describes a basic key-binding scheme for leveling, Q for movement/gap-close skills (Assassination, Flash Slash, Penetration-type skills), E for core damage skills (Heart-piercing, Ambush, Whirlwind Slash), R for conditional/finisher effects (Pattern Explosion), plus Spacebar to help reset the cycle Inven, date unknown8 kr-era. Single source, informal community post, treat as illustrative rather than authoritative.
blocks.tags: assassin rotation combo pve pvp opener

blocks.title: Leveling notes
blocks.bodyHtml:
Assassin levels well once breakpoint skills land around level 20, but needs careful positioning.

Solo leveling comfort: sources agree Assassin can level efficiently once its early breakpoint skills (level 16/20 traits) are secured, but is not considered the most beginner-forgiving class due to its reliance on positioning Overgear, date unknown1 Overgear, date unknown2.

Sustain: PvE-focused guides recommend prioritizing mana recovery and lifesteal-adjacent stigma/skill options during leveling to reduce downtime between pulls pvpbank, date unknown3.

Mob density and leveling phases

One fan-made source splits leveling into two phases:

  • Before level 45: follow main story and orange quest objectives
  • After level 45: shift to collecting Lord-trace skill points and farming Daevanion points from sealed/endgame content Field Manual, date unknown4 (single source)
    • Weekly loop: Wanted Order quests, Abyss accessories, expedition gear, and Transcendence Arcana.
When the class "turns on": no source gave an exact level, but the recurring theme across guides is that Assassin's core identity (rear-attack multipliers, Illusive Clone plus Triniel's Dagger buff-chaining) only comes online once its level-20-ish core skills and matching stigmas are unlocked, implying a slower start than simpler classes. Synthesized from multiple sources above, not a direct quote.
blocks.tags: assassin leveling solo sustain mob density

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.bodyHtml:
Time stealth right before engaging, always attack from behind, and swap builds for PvE vs PvP.

  1. Poor stealth timing, entering stealth too early wastes its duration; it should be used right before the opening attack pvpbank, date unknown1.
  2. Ignoring positioning, most of the class's damage multipliers require back attacks, so failing to reposition constantly caps your DPS pvpbank, date unknown2.
  3. Misusing rune/insignia stacking, detonating stacks with Pattern Explosion at the wrong stack count instead of at full stacks is called out as a major DPS loss pvpbank, date unknown3.
  4. Using the same build/stigma setup for both PvE and PvP instead of swapping loadouts pvpbank, date unknown4.
  5. Spreading Skill Points evenly across all abilities instead of committing to level 16/20 breakpoint skills first Field Manual, date unknown5.
  6. Over-investing in gear that will be replaced almost immediately, instead of pacing enhancement spend to milestone gear u4gm, date unknown6 (could not verify by direct fetch, 403, single source).
  7. Chasing a "perfect" meta build in the first 40 levels instead of just leveling with the core kit pvpbank, date unknown7.
  8. Holding Triniel's Dagger too long, breaking buff-window alignment with your core attack chain, instead of using it in the recommended 3-8 second window Field Manual, date unknown8 (single source).
  9. Letting Illusive Clone/Swift Contract cooldowns drift out of sync instead of chaining them together at the start of a damage window Field Manual, date unknown9 (single source).
  10. Dropping defensive tools (Evasion Stance) too early in a fight, leaving no answer for incoming burst since Assassin has low innate durability, "fragility and short reach" per the class overview aion2hub, date unknown10 Field Manual, date unknown11.
